case_metadata.event: Tencent Cloud AI Agent Hackathon Singapore 2026 — AI Agent Digital Native Track
case_metadata.ruling_rationale: Driver had a legitimate traffic reason to reroute (PIE vehicle fire + heavy congestion at trip start), but failed to inform the rider of the route change per ride-hailing policy. The rider is partially compensated for the excess distance fare ($3.44) attributable to the non-notified deviation. The driver is not fully penalised as the reroute was necessary for safety and efficiency.

dispute_ticket.description: The driver took a significantly longer route from Orchard Central to Changi Airport T3. I normally take the PIE which takes about 35 minutes and costs around $28. On this trip the driver went through Geylang and East Coast area, taking 37 minutes and the fare was $35. The driver did not inform me about any route change or traffic. The extra distance was 4.3 km and I was overcharged. I am requesting a refund of the excess fare.

fare_breakdown.notes: The actual distance of 24.8 km is 4.3 km more than the estimated 20.5 km. The distance fare is calculated at $0.80/km. The excess distance fare attributable to the route deviation is $3.44. Tolls also increased by $2.22 due to the additional ERP gantries and ECP usage. The time difference is minimal (+2 min) suggesting the reroute did not significantly delay the trip, supporting that traffic on PIE was indeed a concern.

gps_telemetry.location_desc: ECP near Bedok / East Coast Park

waypoints.location_desc: Scotts Rd to PIE (Cairnhill) slip road
Changi Airport T3 (dropoff via PIE Exit 2)

optimal_route.notes: This is the system-recommended route via PIE. It is the most direct path from Orchard to Changi Airport T3 under normal traffic conditions. The driver instead took a route through the CBD, Nicoll Highway, Geylang/Old Airport Road, and ECP, adding 4.3 km.

chat_logs.message: Hi! I'm at the Orchard Central main entrance, wearing a blue dress. White Toyota Vios right?
Yes that's me! I can see you, coming now. 1 min.
Great thanks! Heading to Changi T3, my flight is at 3:30pm.
Sure, no problem. We will get there in time.
Hey, are we going the right way? This doesn't look like the usual route to the airport.
Don't worry, I know the way. We will reach on time.

chat_log_analysis.driver_response_content: Don't worry, I know the way. We will reach on time.
chat_log_analysis.analysis: The rider explicitly queried the route at 13:24 (MSG-005) after noticing the deviation near Shenton Way / Nicoll Highway. The driver's response (MSG-006) was dismissive and did not explain the reason for the deviation (PIE traffic). At no point did the driver proactively inform the rider of a route change or cite traffic conditions. This constitutes a failure to meet the driver's notification obligation under ride-hailing policy.

traffic_conditions.stretch: PIE Exit 16 (Cactus / PAYA LEBAR) to Exit 11 (TAMPINES RD)
traffic_conditions.description: Vehicle fire on PIE eastbound between Paya Lebar and Hougang. Lanes 1 and 2 blocked. Heavy congestion and long delays reported from 13:05.

traffic_conditions.road: PIE exit ramp — Changi Airport exit
traffic_conditions.description: Heavy congestion on PIE near the airport exit, likely a secondary effect of the vehicle fire upstream.
ECP eastbound flowing smoothly. No incidents. The driver's reroute through ECP was a reasonable alternative given PIE conditions.

alternative_routes_available: ECP via Nicoll Hwy / Geylang (driver's choice)
Tampines Expressway (TPE) via CTE
Regional routes via Sims Ave / Tanjong Katong
traffic_analysis.reroute_reason: A vehicle fire on PIE eastbound at 13:05 (10 minutes before pickup) made the optimal route impassable for much of the trip window. The driver's decision to reroute via Nicoll Hwy → Geylang → ECP was a reasonable and safety-motivated alternative.
traffic_analysis.notification_gap: The driver did not proactively inform the rider of the route change or the reason (PIE traffic). When the rider explicitly asked about the route at 13:24, the driver's response was dismissive and did not explain the traffic situation.
traffic_analysis.policy_reference: RydeResolve Driver Policy §4.2: 'Drivers must inform the rider of any route deviation from the system-recommended route and the reason for the deviation before or at the point of deviation. Failure to notify renders the driver liable for excess fare charges attributable to the unnotified deviation.'

items.description: GPS trail showing actual route via CBD, Nicoll Hwy, Geylang, ECP — deviation confirmed
Actual fare $35.00 vs estimated $28.50 — excess of $6.50, of which $3.44 is distance fare
Actual distance 24.8 km vs estimated 20.5 km — excess of 4.3 km
Vehicle fire on PIE eastbound at 13:05, 10 min before pickup — route deviation justified
ECP flowing smoothly — alternative route was efficient
No proactive route change notification in chat — rider had to ask; driver response did not cite traffic
Rider queried route at 13:24 — demonstrates awareness and concern; driver response was dismissive
Actual duration 37 min vs estimated 35 min — only 2 min excess, suggesting reroute did not materially delay arrival
Driver avg rating 4.7, 2143 trips, 0 fraud flags — credible and experienced driver

recommended_ruling.rationale: The driver deviated from the optimal PIE route due to a genuine vehicle fire and heavy congestion on PIE eastbound. The reroute to ECP was reasonable and safety-motivated, and the trip duration (37 min) was close to the estimate (35 min). However, the driver failed to inform the rider of the route change as required by Driver Policy §4.2. The rider's query at 13:24 and the driver's dismissive response further confirm the notification failure. A partial refund of the excess distance fare ($3.44) is awarded to the rider. The driver is not penalised for the full excess ($6.50) as the reroute was justified by traffic conditions and did not cause significant delay.

breakdown.note: Only the excess distance fare is refunded. Tolls are passed through at cost. The time difference is minimal and does not warrant additional refund. Surge is applied to the entire trip and is not affected by the route choice.

actions.description: Issue a reminder to the driver about the route deviation notification policy (§4.2). No formal warning given as this is a first notification-related incident and the reroute itself was justified.
Log the notification failure against the driver's route deviation compliance metric for monitoring.
